outline: MHC class II deficiency (bare lymphocyte syndrome type II)
primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
diagnosis: MHC class II deficiency (bare lymphocyte syndrome type II) due to CIITA dysfunction
mechanism: CIITA and the RFX complex are transcriptional regulators required for MHC class II gene expression. Loss of CIITA can abolish MHC II expression on antigen-presenting cells, impairing positive selection and peripheral activation of CD4-positive T cells and causing combined immunodeficiency.
vignette: A 10-month-old boy has recurrent pneumonia, chronic diarrhea, oral candidiasis, and failure to thrive. Flow cytometry shows markedly reduced CD4-positive T cells and nearly absent HLA-DR expression on B cells, while MHC class I expression is preserved. Genetic testing identifies a homozygous loss-of-function variant in CIITA.
lead: Which of the following immune processes is most directly impaired in this child?
correct: Expression of MHC class II molecules required for antigen presentation to CD4-positive T cells
distractors: Transport of cytosolic peptides into the endoplasmic reticulum for loading onto MHC class I
Somatic V(D)J recombination of immunoglobulin and T-cell receptor genes
CD40 ligand signaling from activated T cells to B cells
Negative selection of autoreactive thymocytes through AIRE-dependent tissue-antigen expression
distractor_notes: TAP defects reduce MHC class I peptide loading and primarily affect CD8-positive T-cell biology, not HLA-DR expression.
RAG defects impair lymphocyte receptor rearrangement and cause a different severe combined immunodeficiency phenotype.
CD40L deficiency causes hyper-IgM syndrome but does not abolish HLA-DR/MHC class II expression on B cells.
AIRE defects cause autoimmune polyendocrine syndrome through defective central tolerance rather than absent MHC class II transcription.
key_expl: CIITA is the master transactivator of MHC class II gene expression. CIITA or RFX-complex defects cause MHC class II deficiency (bare lymphocyte syndrome type II), leading to near-absent HLA class II expression and impaired development and activation of CD4-positive T cells.
objective: Explain bare lymphocyte syndrome type II as failure of transcriptional regulation of MHC class II expression, causing defective CD4 T-cell selection and antigen presentation.
